titulo: Swallowed gum does not stay in your stomach for seven years
receta: mito cotidiano con numero para guardar + pregunta de identidad familiar
destinatario: se lo manda un padre o madre a su hijo (o a su pareja) que cree que el chicle tragado se queda siete anos para tranquilizarlo
regla_guardable: One swallowed piece of gum passes in about 40 hours, not seven years. Many pieces, or belly pain and vomiting: call a doctor.

interaccion.guardar: One swallowed piece: about 40 hours, not 7 years. Lots of gum, or belly pain/vomiting: call a doctor.
interaccion.comentar: What did your family tell you would happen if you swallowed gum?

fuentes: Cleveland Clinic, 'What Happens When You Swallow Gum?': the seven-year idea is false; swallowed gum leaves the body in about 40 hours, whole, in stool; gum base can't be broken down by digestion; swallowing lots of gum or doing it every day can cause intestinal blockage
KidsHealth (Nemours), 'Swallowed Gum': the seven-year idea isn't true; swallowing a large mass or many small pieces in a short time can block the digestive tract in rare cases

frases.texto: You swallowed a piece of gum once, and somebody told you it would sit in your stomach for seven years.
frases.estilo: Dry, direct, with a half smile.

frases.texto: Gum base can't be broken down by digestion, so it doesn't get digested at all. It just rides along.
Cleveland Clinic says it comes out whole, about forty hours later.

Heads up: Cleveland Clinic warns that swallowing lots of gum, or doing it every day, can cause a blockage. KidsHealth says blockages from gum are rare. If you get belly pain or vomiting after swallowing a lot, call a doctor.
So one swallowed piece? No panic. Just remind the kids to spit it out.
